_comment: SAMPLE DATA. Illustrative hello-autotools review; not evidence of a live scan. The cover, findings and evidence register are hand-kept illustrations. families, processes, scoring.family_weight, report.pipeline_commit, attack_chains (3A), dependency_reachability (3B), threat_workbench (3C) and each finding's exploit_signal and lane-12 trail row are produced by pipeline/report/sample_data.py through the real code paths (job-graph.json, threat_workbench.join over canned cell replies, the lane-14 and 06 report builders, cvss4.py); run `python3 pipeline/report/sample_data.py` after changing them and never hand-edit those blocks. Math fields are LaTeX and render verbatim in both the PDF and the KaTeX preview. PRE-FIX GAP SET: the hand-kept finding AR-005 and the hand-kept SBOM/SCA/lifecycle gap texts describe hello-autotools before the 2026-10-03 gap punch list (vendored cJSON without purl/CPE, OSV skipped); since 3436f9c (P19) cJSON carries pkg:github/davegamble/cjson and its CPE. See docs/continuation-prompts/2026-10-03-gap-punchlist-hello-autotools.md.

report.title: Application Security Review
report.native_tier_note: clang compiled 6/6 project TUs plus vendored cJSON; IR, CSA/CTU and SVF substrate available (ADR-0001).

processes.gap: No runbooks or monitoring configuration in the target; topology inferred from the Dockerfile only.
No test plan and no test results: nothing to ingest (explicit gap).
No instrumented test run: coverage is missing (explicit gap).
Syft found no package manifest; vendored cJSON 1.7.18 was added from the accepted build-index vendored members without a purl or CPE (inferred component kept as an explicit gap).
Grype ran and matched nothing; OSV was SKIPPED_NA per tool because no component carries a purl. Vendored cJSON was not matched against any advisory.
cJSON 1.7.18 is not in the pinned lifecycle reference table; its lifecycle is reported unknown.
EPSS/KEV not assessed: no pinned offline snapshot has been imported; every exploit signal reads 'not assessed'.

findings.title: Stack buffer overflow: strcpy of CLI name into 32-byte buffer

snippets.note: build_greeting(): buf is 32 bytes; strcpy has no bound.
source: // This is intentional: it is the seeded defect this fixture target
// exists to exercise for source/native SAST and dynamic tools. See
// docs/VULNERABILITIES.md for details and the expected finding.

trail: semgrep strcpy, native-sast CSA, CodeQL cpp
refutation failed: no length check on any path
VERIFIED: copy length is argv-controlled and the buffer is 32 bytes (static)
remediation objective: bounded copy (proposal, not validated)
findings.summary: The greeting "Hello, " + name + "!" is copied into char buf[32] with strcpy. A name of 24 or more characters overflows buf. Reached on every run. A hardened distro build aborts via _FORTIFY_SOURCE; an unhardened or ASan build shows the corruption.
findings.remediation: Return the std::string directly, or use a bounded copy and reject oversize names.
findings.exploit_signal: EPSS/KEV not applicable (not a dependency finding)

findings.title: Format string: CLI-derived message used as printf format

snippets.note: log_message(): message is the format argument.
source: // (e.g. "%x %x %x") or crash the process (e.g. "%s" reading an
// invalid pointer). The fix is `std::printf("%s\n", message.c_str())`.

trail: VERIFIED: CLI-derived text reaches the printf format argument (static)
findings.summary: log_message() passes the greeting, which embeds the CLI name, straight to printf as the format. Conversion specifiers in the name are interpreted.
findings.exploit_signal: EPSS/KEV not applicable (not a dependency finding)

findings.title: OS command injection: name concatenated into system() command

snippets.note: run_report(): no escaping; system(3) runs the string through /bin/sh.
source: // the privileges of this process. There is no shell-metacharacter
// escaping or use of a safer exec* family call with an argv array.

trail: data flow argv -> name -> cmd recorded in IR facts
not refuted; flag gate lowers reachability only
VERIFIED: name is concatenated into the system() command without quoting (static)
findings.summary: With --report, the CLI name is spliced into an echo command and passed to system(). A double quote breaks out of the quoted argument and runs arbitrary shell commands with the process's privileges.
findings.remediation: Write the log line with file I/O instead of a shell, or use execve with an argv array.
findings.exploit_signal: EPSS/KEV not applicable (not a dependency finding)

findings.title: Out-of-bounds write: memcpy behind STORE_INTO macro and template

snippets.note: copy_into_fixed<N>(): copies src.size() bytes into N-byte dst.
source: // this isn't behind glibc's _FORTIFY_SOURCE strcpy checking by
// name -- but memcpy with a compile-time-known destination size is
// still eligible for __memcpy_chk fortification on a hardened
// toolchain, so the same "aborts instead of silently corrupting"
// caveat from VULN-01 can apply here too. See docs/VULNERABILITIES.md.
// The macro layer: call sites use STORE_INTO(...), not
// copy_into_fixed(...) directly, so reaching the vulnerable memcpy
// requires seeing through both this macro expansion and the template

snippets.note: Instantiated as copy_into_fixed<16> through the macro, behind --store.

trail: CodeQL cpp: 0 hits; semgrep: 0 hits; IR facts: memcpy size from input
IR slice: memcpy size = name.size(), dst = 16
refutation failed: no clamp before copy
findings.summary: STORE_INTO expands to copy_into_fixed<16>, which memcpys the whole name into a 16-byte stack slot. Only the tools that see through macro expansion and template instantiation report it; this is the fixture's control for that capability.
findings.remediation: Check src.size() < N before the copy, or truncate explicitly.
findings.exploit_signal: EPSS/KEV not applicable (not a dependency finding)

findings.title: Vendored cJSON 1.7.18 has no purl or CPE; advisory matching could not cover it
trail: syft: no manifest; build index: vendored member (inferred, no purl)
SCA: grype no match, OSV SKIPPED_NA (no purl)
UNRESOLVED: the component has no advisory identity
findings.summary: The build links a vendored cJSON that no manifest declares. 02-sbom-inventory adds it from the accepted build-index vendored members, but without a purl or CPE, so Grype matched nothing and OSV was not applicable. The fixture documents CVE-2025-57052 for this version; this review cannot confirm or clear it. Section 3B has no dependency match to decide, and lane 06 found no call to the JSON-pointer API in project code.
findings.remediation: Give the vendored cJSON a package identity (purl or CPE) so SCA matching covers it, or replace it with a declared dependency.
findings.exploit_signal: EPSS/KEV not assessed (no pinned snapshot imported)

findings.title: Runtime image runs as root; base image not pinned by digest

snippets.note: Final stage: floating tag, no USER before ENTRYPOINT.

trail: hadolint DL3006/DL3002, checkov CKV_DOCKER_3, trivy DS002
findings.summary: Both stages use debian:bookworm-slim by tag, and the runtime stage has no USER instruction, so the binary runs as root. Three scanners agree.
findings.remediation: Pin FROM by digest and add a non-root USER before ENTRYPOINT.
findings.exploit_signal: EPSS/KEV not applicable (not a dependency finding)

findings.title: Unchecked NULL from cJSON_PrintUnformatted used to build std::string

snippets.note: rendered can be NULL on allocation failure.
source: free(rendered); // cJSON allocates with malloc(); must be freed with free(), not delete.

trail: UNRESOLVED: the allocation-failure path needs dynamic evidence the pipeline does not collect
findings.summary: cJSON_PrintUnformatted returns NULL when allocation fails, and std::string(nullptr) is undefined behavior. Only reachable with --json under memory pressure.
findings.remediation: Check rendered for NULL before constructing the string.
findings.exploit_signal: EPSS/KEV not applicable (not a dependency finding)

findings.title: Mismatched deallocation: free() on cJSON output (refuted)

source: free(rendered); // cJSON allocates with malloc(); must be freed with free(), not delete.

trail: REFUTED: cJSON default hooks allocate with malloc; no cJSON_InitHooks call in project
findings.summary: The scanner assumed a C++ allocation. cJSON allocates with malloc by default and the project never installs custom hooks, so free() is correct.
findings.exploit_signal: EPSS/KEV not applicable (not a dependency finding)

privacy_threats.statement: The --report option writes the user-supplied name to a JSON file whose permissions follow the process umask, so other local accounts may be able to read it.
privacy_threats.regulatory_notes: GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) confidentiality may apply if the name is personal data (candidate)

dependency_reachability.reason: 06-cve-reachability had no SCA match to decide
dependency_reachability.note: Dependency reachability is decided by deterministic engines, never by a model: reachable needs a hash-bound witness from CodeQL or the IR/CPG engine; unreachable only from the complete IR/CPG engine with the dependency source analysed; conflict means the engines disagree and is left for review; unknown is a coverage gap, not 'not vulnerable'. A Critical dependency finding requires reachable (ADR-0020).
